candidate.answerReason: The 5×4 ordered choices count each pair twice. No three points are collinear, so the 10 unordered pairs determine 10 distinct lines.

methods.label: Count point pairs without duplication
methods.explanation: Since no three points are collinear, each pair determines a distinct line. Choose the first point in \(5\) ways and the second from the remaining \(4\), giving \(5\times4\) ordered choices. Every pair is counted twice, once in each order, so dividing by \(2\) counts each pair once. There are \(5\times4\div2=10\) lines in total.
methods.levelReason: Uses elementary multiplication and division to count small unordered pairs. The explanation of the two possible orders fits Grade 7 without formal combination notation.

candidate.annotationRationale:
The task assesses how two distinct points determine a line (cnm_054) and how to count small unordered selections (cnm_h236). Both appear in the written method: the no-three-collinear condition makes different pairs determine different lines, and division by two removes the duplicated orders. The cnm_h236 assignment uses only its small unordered-selection criterion, without requiring the general combination formula.
